tools.name: interjson_gate
tools.title: Gate: may I execute this?
tools.description: The execution gate for LLM output. Call this before executing tool arguments or trusting structured output. Returns decision (safe/cosmetic_repair/lossy_repair/ambiguous/invalid), executable, exactness, ambiguity, schema satisfaction, the parsed value, and a retry hint. If `executable` is false, do not execute: send `retry.prompt` back to the model and re-emit the arguments.

text.description: The raw text to inspect: the model's tool arguments, or any JSON document.

profile.description: Safety profile. `agent` (default here) refuses a lossy or ambiguous repair instead of guessing; `permissive` repairs for display; `strict` refuses any repair.

schema_json.description: The tool's declared inputSchema, passed through unchanged (type/properties/required/items/enum/const/minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern). Unsupported keywords are refused, not ignored.

business_authorized.description: Always `false`: the gate checks JSON and the declared schema, never path/URL/permission/business authorization. A host must apply its own policy before executing (audit §7.1).

retry.description: Present when `executable` is false: `code`, `prompt` and `kind` (why the refusal cannot be retried the same way).

refusal.description: `null` when executable; otherwise `kind` (syntax / schema_or_intent / host_declaration / provider) and `auto_retry`.

tools.name: interjson_repair
tools.title: Repair malformed JSON
tools.description: Repair malformed JSON (markdown fences, single quotes, comments, trailing commas, Python literals, truncated values) and return the repaired text with the exactness label and the repair records. Use this when you need the document, not a decision.

text.description: The raw text to inspect: the model's tool arguments, or any JSON document.

profile.description: Safety profile. `agent` (default here) refuses a lossy or ambiguous repair instead of guessing; `permissive` repairs for display; `strict` refuses any repair.

schema_json.description: The tool's declared inputSchema, passed through unchanged (type/properties/required/items/enum/const/minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern). Unsupported keywords are refused, not ignored.

tools.name: interjson_validate
tools.title: Validate without repairing
tools.description: Report whether text is legal JSON and, when a declaration is given, whether it satisfies it. This never repairs: a document that could be fixed is still reported as invalid, with the repair the lenient profile would make.

text.description: The raw text to inspect: the model's tool arguments, or any JSON document.

schema_json.description: The tool's declared inputSchema, passed through unchanged (type/properties/required/items/enum/const/minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern). Unsupported keywords are refused, not ignored.

tools.name: interjson_readiness
tools.title: When do fields become final?
tools.description: Given a declaration, report when each required field becomes final in the stream: syntax/schema/settled fractions and the missing members. Use this to stop a generation early when the arguments are already settled.

text.description: The raw text to inspect: the model's tool arguments, or any JSON document.

schema_json.description: The tool's declared inputSchema, passed through unchanged (type/properties/required/items/enum/const/minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/minLength/maxLength/pattern). Unsupported keywords are refused, not ignored.

result.instructions:
InterJSON is a local execution gate for model output. It runs on this machine over stdio and performs no network requests.

Before executing tool arguments or trusting structured output, call `interjson_gate` with the raw argument text and the tool's inputSchema as `schema_json`.
- `executable: true` means the arguments are safe to execute; `value` is the parsed object.
- `executable: false` means do not execute: send `retry.prompt` back to the model and use the re-emitted arguments.

`interjson_repair` returns repaired text, `interjson_validate` reports legality without repairing, and `interjson_readiness` reports when streaming fields become final.
